deferred_follow_up: Signed execution-nonce single-use enforcement has real mutation evidence, but native-channel replay resistance remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP for deployments that do not require sender-constrained DPoP or use only process-local replay state. The conformance test closes same-process replay after a nonce has been validated and consumed. It does not prove nonce uniqueness across restart or failover, coordinate replay state across multiple kernel processes, or prevent replay of non-DPoP grants within their validity window. Follow-up work must require DPoP for replay-sensitive profiles and qualify a durable shared nonce store under restart, failover, and concurrent-consumption tests.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/native_channel_replay.rs mints a production SignedExecutionNonce, verifies and consumes it once, then requires the second presentation to fail with ExecutionNonceError::Replayed. Separate arms reject tool-binding mutation and signed-body tampering. A targeted cargo-mutants run replaced chio_kernel::execution_nonce::reserve_execution_nonce with Ok(()); this removed replay-store consumption while preserving validation, and the second-presentation assertion caught the bypass. PARTIAL: durable multi-process replay state, restart and failover continuity, and mandatory DPoP for replay-sensitive native profiles remain deferred.
